name: Santa Barbara Foundation Conservation, Environment and Public Trails Grants
summary: Grants to nonprofits serving Santa Barbara County for land conservation, community-based habitat and wetland restoration, threatened-species work and public trail projects.

eligibility.rule: Serves Santa Barbara County and has operated there for at least 1 year
Demonstrates sound fiscal management and financial sustainability
Is a 501(c)(3) organization or uses a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor
Serves as the primary project lead, not a government agency or private landowner
Secures or processes all required permits and landowner approvals for public trails projects
Public trails projects: funded scope is completed within the grant period
Not fully education-focused, endowment, advocacy/lobbying, or land buys under 90% funded

documents: Board roster, if using a fiscal sponsor
Organizational financial summary, if using a fiscal sponsor
Fiscal sponsorship letter agreement, if applicable

applicant_types.quote: Organizations must be certified as tax exempt under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code or use a fiscal sponsor with 501(c)(3) tax status.

geography.quote: Organizations must serve Santa Barbara County and have at least one (1) year of operations in the County.

access.quote: Organizations must implement new or existing projects to address conservation, environment, and/or public trails

amount.quote: The maximum award for Conservation, Environment and Public Trails grants is $25,000.

fiscal_sponsor.quote: Organizations must be certified as tax exempt under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code or use a fiscal sponsor with 501(c)(3) tax status.

effort.quote: Applications must be submitted through our SmartSimple grant application, which includes the following documents:

eligibility.quote: Organizations must serve Santa Barbara County and have at least one (1) year of operations in the County.
Organizations must demonstrate sound fiscal management (e.g., financial audits/reviews, board oversight) and financial sustainability (e.g., diversified funding, reserves).
Organizations must be certified as tax exempt under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code or use a fiscal sponsor with 501(c)(3) tax status.

Direct support to government agencies or private landowners (grantees must be a 501(c)(3) organization and serve as the primary project lead agency; public or private entities may be part of a collaboration);
All permits and landowner approvals required to implement the proposed project must be secured or formally in process at the time of application.
Projects may be part of a larger, longer-term effort, but the specific scope funded by this grant must reach completion within the grant period.

Projects that are 100% education focused; Direct purchase of land or easements that have raised less than 90% of funds required; Direct support to government agencies or private landowners (grantees must be a 501(c)(3) organization and serve as the primary project lead agency; public or private entities may be part of a collaboration); Endowment; Advocacy and lobbying activities.

after_award.quote: The grant period is up to one year from the award date and reporting requirement will be noted in the award letter.

documents.quote: Organizational profile Program Budget Form Narrative answering seven (7) questions
including a board roster and organizational financial summary, where applicable, for both the fiscal sponsor and the sponsored organization.
A copy of the letter of agreement entered into with the sponsored organization is also required.
